lessons.title: Making Healthy Choices
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to identify a healthy food choice.
lessons.starter_activity: Sort a basket of real/plastic foods into healthy/treat.
lessons.main_activity: Discuss balanced choices; children build a paper plate meal using healthy food pictures.
key_questions: Why is this food healthy?
What did you put on your plate?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note understanding of healthy choices — evidence for PSED.2.
lessons.home_link: Help choose a healthy snack at home.

lessons.title: Talking About Favourite Foods
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe a favourite food using descriptive words.
lessons.starter_activity: Adult models describing a favourite food.
lessons.main_activity: Children describe a favourite food to a partner using taste/texture words.
key_questions: What does it taste/feel like?
Why is it your favourite?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note descriptive vocabulary — evidence for CL.2.
lessons.home_link: Describe your favourite meal to family.

lessons.title: Exercise Circuit
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to complete a range of exercise movements with control.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss why exercise is good for us.
lessons.main_activity: Rotate through simple exercise stations: star jumps, hopping, stretching.
key_questions: How does your body feel after exercise?
Which was trickiest?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note stamina and control — evidence for PD.1.
lessons.plenary: Cool down and discuss how bodies feel.
lessons.home_link: Do a mini exercise circuit together at home.

lessons.title: Phonics: Introducing 'g'
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to say the sound 'g' and blend words (gap, dig, mug).
lessons.starter_activity: Recap sounds learned so far.
lessons.main_activity: Introduce 'g' sound/action; blend new CVC words.
key_questions: What sound is this?
Can you blend g-a-p?
lessons.assessment_notes: Update phonics tracker for 'g'.
lessons.home_link: Practise blending gap, dig, mug.

lessons.title: Counting Fruit Portions
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to count fruit pieces up to 10 accurately.
lessons.starter_activity: Count fruit pieces in a bowl together.
lessons.main_activity: Children count and sort real/play fruit into groups, recording totals.
key_questions: How many pieces are there?
Can you count them again to check?
lessons.assessment_notes: Record counting accuracy — evidence for MATHS.1.
lessons.home_link: Count fruit pieces at home.

lessons.title: Where Does Food Come From?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to identify whether a food comes from a plant or an animal.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss where milk comes from as an example.
lessons.main_activity: Sort food picture cards into 'from a plant' / 'from an animal' groups.
key_questions: Where does this food come from?
Does it grow or come from an animal?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note early scientific categorisation — evidence for UTW.3.
lessons.plenary: Recap food origins as a class.
lessons.home_link: Talk about where tonight's dinner ingredients come from.

lessons.title: Fruit and Vegetable Printing
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to use fruit/vegetable halves to make printed patterns.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at the cut cross-section of an apple/orange.
lessons.main_activity: Children dip fruit/veg halves in paint and print patterns on paper.
key_questions: What shape does this print make?
Can you make a pattern?
lessons.assessment_notes: Observe pattern-making and material exploration — evidence for EAD.1.
lessons.home_link: Look at fruit/veg cross-sections at home before eating.

lessons.title: How Exercise Makes Us Feel
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe how their body/mood feels after exercise.
lessons.starter_activity: Do a quick burst of jumping jacks.
lessons.main_activity: Discuss and draw how their body feels after exercise (heart racing, happy, tired).
key_questions: How does your heart feel now?
Do you feel happy after exercise?

differentiation.extension: Explain why exercise creates that feeling

lessons.assessment_notes: Note body-awareness language — evidence for PSED.1.
lessons.home_link: Notice how you feel after playing outside today.

lessons.title: Following a Recipe: Listening for Order
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to follow simple sequential instructions for a recipe.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap sequencing words.
lessons.main_activity: Follow a simple no-cook recipe (e.g. fruit skewers) step by step as a class, listening carefully to each instruction.
key_questions: What do we do first?
What comes next?

differentiation.extension: Repeat back the next step before doing it

lessons.assessment_notes: Note sequencing and listening skill — evidence for CL.1.
lessons.home_link: Help follow a simple recipe step at home.

lessons.title: Ball Skills: Kicking and Aiming
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to kick a ball towards a target with increasing accuracy.
lessons.starter_activity: Practise gentle kicking against a wall.
lessons.main_activity: Set up simple targets (cones/hoops); children practise kicking a ball towards them.
key_questions: How do you aim the ball?
Did you hit the target?

differentiation.extension: Increase distance or reduce target size

lessons.assessment_notes: Note ball control progress — evidence for PD.1.
lessons.home_link: Practise kicking a ball at a target outside.

lessons.title: Story Time: 'Oliver's Vegetables'
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to answer a 'why' question about a character's choices.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss a vegetable children are unsure about.
lessons.main_activity: Read 'Oliver's Vegetables' (or similar), discussing why Oliver's feelings about vegetables change.
key_questions: Why didn't Oliver like vegetables at first?
Why did his feelings change?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note reasoning and comprehension — evidence for LIT.1.
lessons.home_link: Try one new vegetable this week.

lessons.title: Number Bonds to 5 with Snacks
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to find combinations that make 5 using snack counters.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap making 5 from Week 3.
lessons.main_activity: Using snack-shaped counters, children find different combinations making 5 and record with drawings.
key_questions: What two groups make 5?
Can you find another way?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note number bond progress — evidence for MATHS.1.
lessons.plenary: Class collects all ways to make 5.
lessons.home_link: Find ways to make 5 with snacks at home.

lessons.title: Growing Our Own Food
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe what a plant needs to grow.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at a seed and discuss what it might become.
lessons.main_activity: Plant a fast-growing seed (e.g. cress) in a pot, discussing what it will need to grow.
key_questions: What does a plant need to grow?
What do you think will happen?

differentiation.extension: Child predicts growth and records over time

lessons.assessment_notes: Note understanding of plant needs — evidence for UTW.3.
lessons.plenary: Set up a watering rota for the class plant.
lessons.home_link: Water a plant together at home if you have one.

lessons.title: Role-Play: Class Café Healthy Menu
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to create and use an imaginative healthy food menu in role-play.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the café role-play from Week 1.
lessons.main_activity: Children design a 'healthy specials' menu for the café and role-play taking healthy food orders.
resources_needed: Role-play café area, paper for menus
key_questions: What healthy food is on your menu?
What would you like to order?

differentiation.extension: Child invents and prices new healthy dishes

lessons.assessment_notes: Observe imaginative language and healthy food knowledge — evidence for EAD.2/UTW.3.
lessons.home_link: Help plan a healthy meal at home.

lessons.title: Brushing Teeth and Hygiene
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to explain why we brush our teeth.
lessons.starter_activity: Sing a tooth-brushing song.
lessons.main_activity: Discuss and practise (with model teeth/toothbrush) correct brushing technique and why it matters.
key_questions: Why do we brush our teeth?
How many times a day should we brush?

differentiation.extension: Explain what happens if we don't brush

lessons.assessment_notes: Note hygiene understanding — evidence for PSED.2.
lessons.home_link: Practise brushing teeth correctly tonight.

lessons.title: Explaining Why Exercise Is Good
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to explain a reason exercise is good for us using 'because'.
lessons.starter_activity: Adult models: 'Exercise is good because it makes my heart strong.'
lessons.main_activity: Children complete and share their own 'Exercise is good because ___' sentences.
key_questions: Why is exercise good for us?
What happens to your body when you exercise?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note causal language use — evidence for CL.2.
lessons.plenary: Class list of reasons exercise is good.
lessons.home_link: Explain to family why exercise is important.

lessons.title: Yoga for Calm Bodies
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to hold simple yoga poses with balance and control.
lessons.starter_activity: Deep breathing warm-up.
lessons.main_activity: Practise simple yoga poses (tree, cat, downward dog) with adult demonstration.
key_questions: How does this pose feel?
Can you hold it steady?

differentiation.extension: Hold poses longer, link poses in sequence

lessons.assessment_notes: Note balance and body control — evidence for PD.1.
lessons.plenary: Relaxation lying down to calm music.
lessons.home_link: Try a yoga pose together at home.

lessons.title: Phonics: Introducing 'o'
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to say the sound 'o' and blend words (dog, pot, mop).
lessons.starter_activity: Recap sounds learned so far.
lessons.main_activity: Introduce 'o' sound/action; blend new CVC words.
key_questions: What sound is this?
Can you blend d-o-g?
lessons.assessment_notes: Update phonics tracker for 'o'.
lessons.home_link: Practise blending dog, pot, mop.

lessons.title: Doubling with Snacks
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to double a small number using concrete objects.
lessons.starter_activity: Show 2 counters, ask 'what is double 2?'
lessons.main_activity: Children double small quantities of snack counters (1-5) and record with drawings.
key_questions: What is double 3?
How did you work it out?

differentiation.extension: Double numbers up to 5 and explain method

lessons.assessment_notes: Note early doubling understanding — evidence for MATHS.2.
lessons.home_link: Practise doubling small amounts of snacks/toys.

lessons.title: Keeping Our Bodies Healthy: Rest and Sleep
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to explain why sleep is important for our bodies.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss how we feel when tired vs rested.
lessons.main_activity: Discuss why sleep helps our bodies and brains; children sequence a bedtime routine.
key_questions: Why do we need sleep?
What helps you sleep well?

differentiation.extension: Explain why each step helps sleep

lessons.assessment_notes: Note understanding of rest/health link — evidence for UTW.3/PSED.2.
lessons.home_link: Follow a calm bedtime routine tonight.

lessons.title: Exercise Dance Routine
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to perform a sequence of exercise movements to music.
lessons.starter_activity: Warm-up free dance.
lessons.main_activity: Learn and perform a simple exercise dance routine (jump, stretch, wiggle) to upbeat music.
key_questions: What movement comes next in the routine?
How does the music make you move?

differentiation.extension: Add an original movement to the routine

lessons.assessment_notes: Note sequencing and expressive movement — evidence for EAD.2/PD.1.
lessons.plenary: Perform the routine together once more.
lessons.home_link: Do the exercise dance routine with family.

lessons.title: Being a Healthy Team
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to work cooperatively in a team health challenge.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss what makes a good team.
lessons.main_activity: Team relay carrying 'healthy food' beanbags to a basket, encouraging teamwork and cheering.
key_questions: How did your team work together?
How did you support your teammates?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note cooperative behaviour — evidence for PSED.3.
lessons.home_link: Play a team game with family/friends.

lessons.title: Describing a Healthy Meal I'd Cook
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe an imaginary healthy meal using full sentences.
lessons.starter_activity: Adult describes a simple healthy meal.
lessons.main_activity: Children describe a healthy meal they would cook, including ingredients, using full sentences.
key_questions: What would you cook?
What ingredients would you use?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note sentence complexity — evidence for CL.2.
lessons.plenary: Share meal ideas as a class 'healthy cookbook' list.
lessons.home_link: Help plan a healthy meal with family this week.

lessons.title: Making Fruit Kebabs (Fine Motor)
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to thread soft fruit pieces onto a skewer safely.
lessons.starter_activity: Wash hands and discuss food safety.
lessons.main_activity: (Allergy-checked) children thread soft fruit pieces onto blunt skewers/sticks to make a healthy snack.
key_questions: Can you thread the fruit carefully?
What fruits did you choose?

differentiation.extension: Create a patterned fruit kebab independently

lessons.assessment_notes: Observe fine motor control and safety awareness — evidence for PD.2.
lessons.plenary: Enjoy eating the fruit kebabs together (if permitted).
lessons.home_link: Help prepare a healthy snack at home.

lessons.title: Writing a Shopping List
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to attempt to write simple food words for a shopping list.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss what a shopping list is for.
lessons.main_activity: Children write/draw a simple healthy shopping list using known phonics sounds.
key_questions: What food will you write?
What sound does that word start with?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note writing progress — evidence for LIT.3.
lessons.plenary: Share shopping lists with a partner.
lessons.home_link: Help write the family shopping list.

lessons.title: Weighing Fruit and Vegetables
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to compare weight using balance scales.
lessons.starter_activity: Hold two objects and guess which is heavier.
lessons.main_activity: Use balance scales to compare weights of different fruits/vegetables, predicting before checking.
key_questions: Which do you think is heavier?
Were you right?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note early measurement understanding — evidence for MATHS.2.
lessons.plenary: Class recap of heaviest/lightest items found.
lessons.home_link: Compare weights of items at home (e.g. in your hands).

lessons.title: Checking on Our Growing Seeds
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to observe and describe changes in their planted seed.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap what was planted on Tuesday.
lessons.main_activity: Children observe and record (drawing) any changes in their cress/seed pots, discussing what's happening.
key_questions: What has changed?
What do you think will happen next?

differentiation.support: Adult prompts what to look for

lessons.assessment_notes: Note observational and scientific language — evidence for UTW.3.
lessons.home_link: Check on any plants growing at home.

lessons.title: Healthy Food Collage
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to create a collage representing a balanced plate of food.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap Monday's balanced plate discussion.
lessons.main_activity: Children cut/tear and stick pictures of healthy foods onto a paper plate template to create a balanced meal collage.
key_questions: What food groups are on your plate?
Is your plate balanced?

differentiation.extension: Explain why the plate is balanced

lessons.assessment_notes: Observe understanding of balanced eating — evidence for EAD.1/UTW.3.
lessons.home_link: Help plan a balanced plate for dinner tonight.

lessons.title: Celebrating Healthy Choices
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to reflect on one healthy choice they made this week.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the week's healthy learning.
lessons.main_activity: Children share one healthy choice they made or learned about this week, adding to a 'Healthy Heroes' wall.
key_questions: What healthy choice did you make?
How do you feel about it?

differentiation.extension: Explain why the choice was healthy

lessons.assessment_notes: Note reflective self-awareness — evidence for PSED.1.
lessons.home_link: Make one healthy choice with your family this weekend.

lessons.title: Healthy Me Quiz Game
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to answer recall questions about healthy habits learned this week.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the week's key vocabulary.
lessons.main_activity: Quiz game asking recall questions about food, exercise, hygiene, and sleep from the week.
key_questions: Why is exercise good for us?
What should we do before bed?
lessons.assessment_notes: Assess recall and listening comprehension — evidence for CL.1.
lessons.home_link: Quiz your family on healthy habits.

lessons.title: Mini Sports Day: Healthy Bodies Challenge
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to combine running, jumping, and ball skills in a fun challenge.
lessons.starter_activity: Warm-up jog and stretch.
lessons.main_activity: Mini sports challenge combining running relay, jumping, and ball kicking stations from the week.
key_questions: Which station used the most energy?
What skill did you use here?
lessons.assessment_notes: Summarise week 5 PD progress — evidence for PD.1.
lessons.plenary: Cool down and celebrate all achievements.
lessons.home_link: Have a mini sports challenge with family.

lessons.title: Phonics Review: All 10 Sounds
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to blend and read CVC words using all sounds learned so far.
lessons.starter_activity: Quick-fire flashcard review of all 10 sounds.
lessons.main_activity: Phonics stations: word-building, CVC reading cards, simple sentence reading (e.g. 'a dog sat').
key_questions: Can you build and read this word?
Can you read this sentence?
lessons.assessment_notes: Finalise week 5 phonics tracker.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate all sounds learned with a reading game.
lessons.home_link: Practise reading simple sentences over the weekend.

lessons.title: Maths Review: Counting, Doubling, Weighing
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to apply counting, doubling, and weight-comparison skills learned this week.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the week's maths vocabulary.
lessons.main_activity: Rotate through 3 stations: counting fruit, doubling snacks, weighing objects.
key_questions: How many is that?
What is double this number?
Which is heavier?
lessons.assessment_notes: Summarise week 5 maths observations.
lessons.plenary: Class recap game combining all three skills.
lessons.home_link: Continue practising counting and doubling over the weekend.

lessons.title: Healthy Me Recap: What We Learned
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to summarise what keeps our bodies healthy.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the week's UTW learning.
lessons.main_activity: Class discussion synthesising food, exercise, hygiene, and sleep learning into a 'Being Healthy' poster.
key_questions: What have we learned keeps us healthy?
What will you do differently now?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note synthesis of the week's learning — evidence for UTW.3.
lessons.home_link: Share the healthy habits you learned with your family.

lessons.title: Healthy Me Celebration Song and Dance
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to perform a learned routine confidently celebrating the week's theme.
lessons.starter_activity: Warm-up with the exercise dance from Wednesday.
lessons.main_activity: Perform the week's exercise dance routine as a 'Healthy Me' celebration for another class/group.
key_questions: What was your favourite part of this week?
How did it feel to perform?
lessons.assessment_notes: Observe confidence and enjoyment — evidence for EAD.2.
lessons.plenary: Round of applause; recap the healthy week.
lessons.home_link: Perform the routine for family this weekend.
